messages.content: Tell me some of the major airports in the United States.

message.content:
Here’s an overview of several of the largest and most significant commercial airports across the United States—ranked roughly by passenger traffic (pre‑COVID) and/or strategic importance: | Airport | City / State | IATA Code | Key Highlights | |---------|--------------|-----------|----------------| | **Hartsfield–Jackson Atlanta International** | Atlanta, GA | ATL | • Largest U.S. airport by enplanements (~110 M passengers).
• Major hub for Delta Air Lines; one of the world’s busiest transfer hubs. | | **Los Angeles International** | Los Angeles, CA | LAX | • Primary gateway to Asia & Oceania from the West Coast.
• Hub for American Airlines, Southwest, JetBlue, Alaska Airlines. | | **Chicago O’Hare International** | Chicago, IL | ORD | • Historically the world's busiest airport (by total flights).
• Joint hub for United and American airlines. | | **Dallas/Fort Worth International** | Dallas–Fort Worth, TX | DFW | • One of only three U.S. airports serving more than 70 M annual passengers.
• Main hub for American Airlines. | | **Denver International** | Denver, CO | DEN | • Largest single-runway airport worldwide.
• Growing hub for United, Frontier, Southwest. | | **John F. Kennedy International** | New York City, NY | JFK | • East coast flagship for many carriers including Delta, United, American, JetBlue. | | **San Francisco International** | San Francisco, CA | SFO | • Strong Asian connections; key hub for United and Alaska Airlines. | | **Seattle/Tacoma International** | Seattle, WA | SEA | • Gateway to Pacific Northwest & Asia; main hub for Alaska Airlines. | | **Orlando International** | Orlando, FL | MCO | • Major leisure destination; high seasonal traffic due to theme parks. | | **Miami International** | Miami, FL | MIA | • Critical link to Latin America/Caribbean; hub for American, LATAM, Avianca. | | **Phoenix Sky Harbor** | Phoenix, AZ | PHX | • Fastest-growing U.S. airport; primary hub for American and Southwest. | | **Charlotte Douglas International** | Charlotte, NC | CLT | • Important hub for American Airlines on the Southeast corridor. | | **Houston Hobby & George Bush Intercontinental** | Houston, TX | HOU/HOU? Actually HOU=George Bush Intercontinental, HOG=Hobby | • Two major airports servicing different carrier mixes; Gulf region hub. | | **Washington Reagan National** | Washington DC | DCA | • Focuses on domestic short-haul routes; hub for United Express, American Eagle. | | **Boston Logan International** | Boston, MA | BOS | • Northeast hub for JetBlue, Delta, United. | ### Why These Airports Matter 1. **Passenger Volume:** They handle tens of millions of travelers annually, making them critical nodes in both national and international air transport networks. 2. **Hub Status:** Most serve as operational bases (“hubs”) for at least one major airline, enabling efficient flight scheduling and connectivity. 3. **Geographic Reach:** Their locations provide access to distinct regions – e.g., Atlantic vs. Pacific coasts, Midwest cross‑country corridors, Southern gateways to Latin America. 4. **Economic Impact:** Beyond transportation, they generate substantial local employment, support tourism, and drive regional economic development. 5. **Infrastructure Scale:** Many feature extensive runway systems, cargo facilities, and advanced navigation aids capable of handling heavy aircraft like the Boeing 747, Airbus A380, and wide‑body freighters. --- #### Quick Reference List (Alphabetical) ``` ATL - Atlanta, GA BOS - Boston, MA CLT - Charlotte, NC DEN - Denver, CO DFW - Dallas/Fort Worth, TX DHS - Detroit Metropolitan (not listed above but also very busy) EWR - Newark Liberty (NYC area) FLL - Fort Lauderdale-Hollywood (Florida) GSO - Greensboro (North Carolina) IAD - Washington Dulles (International) JFK - John F. Kennedy (New York) LAS - McCarran (Las Vegas) LAX - Los Angeles (California) ORD - Chicago O'Hare (Illinois) PHX - Phoenix Sky Harbor (Arizona) SEA - Seattle-Tacoma (Washington) SFO - San Francisco (California) STL - St. Louis Lambert (Missouri) TPA - Tampa Bay (Florida) YUL - Montreal (Canada, often used by U.S. carriers) ``` Feel free to let me know if you’d like deeper data on a particular airport (e.g., terminal layout, recent expansion projects, or specific airline operations)!
